news.headline: Shuklaphanta teams spend two days hunting a rogue elephant to fit a satellite collar near Bhimdatta settlements
news.why_it_matters: The bull has wrecked three buffer-zone homes in a week and killed a woman in Bhimdatta-14 last year; a working collar would let rangers warn villages before it arrives.

news.headline: Dadeldhura police log 27 online fraud complaints and Rs 2.5 million lost in four months, with festival cases rising
news.why_it_matters: Fake bargain ads, job fees, prize calls and fake bank staff asking for OTPs are reaching far-west families; people aged 20 to 40 are hit most.

news.headline: About 68% of farmed land in Dadeldhura has no irrigation, so most fields lie empty through winter
news.why_it_matters: Over 9,000 hectares of arable land sit unused; experts point to irrigation, cold-hardy crops and crop protection as the fix.

news.headline: Dr KC ends his 25th hunger strike after a six-point deal that lets Sudurpashchim's Dasharath Chand health university run MBBS
news.why_it_matters: Seat numbers come later, an ordinance on who can lead the university is due within two weeks, and a probe will check Army Medical College seat increases.

news.headline: Nepal wins its first gold at the Junior International Astronomy Olympiad, plus a bronze and an honourable mention
news.why_it_matters: Students picked through the National Astronomy Olympiad show Nepali school science can compete globally, and the selection route is open to any school.

news.headline: Army helicopter flies a newborn with breathing trouble from Bajura to an ICU in Surkhet
news.why_it_matters: It is the second postnatal airlift from Bajura in four days under the President's Women Upliftment Programme, showing how thin newborn care is in the hills.

news.headline: 25 young developers in Birgunj build working apps in an EU-funded AI-assisted coding bootcamp; Pokhara is next
news.why_it_matters: Leapfrog Connect and the chamber of commerce ran it under the CODE youth digital jobs project, a model a far-west school or chamber could host.

news.headline: Saudi Arabia bars or caps foreigners in 97 tourism and office job titles; about 400,000 Nepalis work there
news.why_it_matters: Reception, travel, HR and clerical jobs shrink for Nepali workers, while technical and physical trades are less affected.

news.headline: Government shows business groups 474 proposed changes across 59 investment and infrastructure laws
news.why_it_matters: FNCCI, CNI and hotel owners will send written comments before the December Infrastructure Summit, which focuses on public-private partnerships.

news.headline: Sugar stocks cover Tihar at Rs 100-110 a kilo, but the LPG shortage that began in February continues
news.why_it_matters: Gas demand rises as it gets colder; dealers blame low imports while the oil corporation blames slow distribution.

news.headline: Laxmi Puja power demand expected to peak at 1,700 MW against about 2,500 MW of generation
news.why_it_matters: Peak festival demand has grown about 400 MW in four years, and home generation alone can now cover it.

news.headline: Tihar flower trade estimated at Rs 645 million, from more than 325 hectares of farms
news.why_it_matters: Floriculture investment now tops Rs 11.5 billion, with marigold the biggest seller and globe amaranth rising.

news.headline: SEBON drafts rules for same-day share trading and asks for public comments
news.why_it_matters: Only liquid, well-run shares would qualify, and brokers would need Rs 200 million capital and risk systems to offer it.

watch.disclaimer: A rules-based screen built from published quarterly reports and the latest closing price. It is not investment advice, not an official rating and not a recommendation to buy or sell.
watch.method: Score out of 100: earnings yield (EPS / price) 35%, return on equity (EPS / book value) 30%, price-to-book, lower is better, 15%, and year-on-year profit growth 20%, each ranked against the other stocks in the list. Minus 15 if bad loans (NPL) are above 6%, minus 7 if 5-6%, minus 10 if distributable profit is negative. Screen leaders are the top three with no warning flags.
watch.universe: Listed banks that have published Q1 FY 2083/84 results so far. More companies are added as their quarterly reports come out.

invest.disclaimer: Projections apply fixed yearly rates and are not promises. Real returns vary year to year, and market options can lose money. This is general information, not investment advice; talk to a licensed adviser before investing.

inflation.note: Latest year-on-year inflation (mid-August to mid-September 2026). Last fiscal year averaged about 2.9%.

options.access: Locked for the term; breaking it early costs interest.
options.basis: Lowest (3.40%), average (4.01%) and highest (4.50%) published fixed deposit rates at commercial banks for Kartik 2083. Rates reset when the deposit renews.
options.name: Bank fixed deposit
options.tax_note: 6% tax is withheld on interest each year.

options.access: Sold only during government issue windows (minimum Rs 10,000); held to maturity.
options.basis: Fixed 7% coupon of the last issue, paid every six months. New issues may pay a different rate, and after 5 years the money is assumed to be reinvested at the same rate.
options.detail: Government of Nepal, 5-year bond, last issue February 2025
options.name: Citizen savings bond
options.tax_note: Interest is taxed at source like deposit interest; 6% assumed.

options.access: Sold only during issue windows; eligibility rules apply.
options.basis: 8.5% coupon of the February 2025 issue. Only Nepalis in foreign employment, or recently returned, can buy, in their own or a family member's name.
options.detail: Government of Nepal, 5-year bond for migrant workers and returnees
options.name: Foreign employment savings bond
options.tax_note: Tax treatment varies by issue; 6% assumed. Some issues have been tax-free.

options.access: Sell any trading day, but prices swing and can stay low for years.
options.basis: Low: no growth. Expected: 4.31% a year, the index's growth over the last 10 years (1,718 in mid-July 2016 to 2,655.22 on 6 Nov 2026). High: 8.69% a year, the long-run average over about 22 years. Price growth only; dividends would add to these figures, and some years lose money.
options.detail: A spread of listed shares that moves with the NEPSE index
options.name: NEPSE shares
options.tax_note: Capital gains tax 3.75% if held over 365 days, 5% otherwise (from 22 Sept 2026). Broker fees not included.

options.access: Sell any day at the dealer's buying rate.
options.basis: Assumed rates. Gold rose about 73% in 2025 (Rs 151,000 to Rs 261,000 a tola) and about 8% so far in 2026; it jumped Rs 13,300 on 5 Nov, fell Rs 5,900 on 6 Nov and ended the week Rs 2,700 higher. Spikes like 2025 rarely repeat, and gold can fall for years.
options.detail: Fine gold, Rs 283,000 a tola in the week to 7 Nov 2026
options.name: Gold
options.tax_note: Tax not modeled. Making charges on jewellery and the dealer's buy-sell gap are not included.

options.access: Slow to sell; can take months, and prices vary plot by plot.
options.basis: Assumed rates. Nepal has no reliable land price index; the central bank stopped its price survey in 2022 because the data could not be trusted. Prices have fallen in slumps (about a third in Kathmandu Valley plots in 2012) and stalled in 2022-25, while deals recovered in 2025/26: transaction value rose to Rs 720.86 billion from Rs 386.15 billion. Rent is not included.
options.detail: A plot or house bought to hold and sell later
options.name: Land and property
options.tax_note: Capital gains tax 7.5% if held more than 5 years, 10% if 5 years or less (budget 2083/84). A 4% buying cost is assumed for the registration fee, which runs about 3-5.3% in Kathmandu Valley and is 25-30% lower for women buyers.

options.access: Slow to sell, and the building needs a manager and upkeep.
options.basis: Assumed: 60% of the money buys land, which grows at the land rates; 40% builds rooms or shops, held at what they cost to build. Rent after upkeep and empty months is assumed at 2%, 3% or 4% of the money put in each year, kept at the same rupee amount, and saved in a fixed deposit at the average rate. Check real rents nearby before relying on these.
options.detail: Land with rooms or shops built to rent out, such as student housing
options.name: Land plus rental building
options.tax_note: 10% local tax on rent; capital gains 7.5% if held more than 5 years, 10% otherwise, when sold.

places.note: Places where published data or big projects point to rising demand for land. Transaction figures count deals, not prices per plot. The outlook is Claude's reading of the drivers and risks, not a price forecast or advice; check local prices, title and access roads before buying.

drivers: Provincial capital with a new health sciences university in Geta, which got its first 90 seats, including 50 MBBS, in October 2026.
Irrigation expansion in Kailali, with Rs 1.33 billion of tenders out and more planned.
Rani Jamara Kulariya irrigation is about three-quarters built.
places.name: Dhangadhi
risks: The planned airport runway extension stalled and is under an anti-corruption investigation.
Sudurpashchim still has among the fewest property deals of any province.
places.signal: Property deals rose 73.16% in the April-July 2026 quarter, the fastest growth of any sub-metropolitan city.

drivers: Nepal and India are expected to mark the start of an integrated check post at Dodhara Chandani, and open a road bridge over the Mahakali, during PM Shah's India visit around 22 November 2026.

The four-lane Mahakali bridge and an 8 km six-lane access road are already built; the port's 42-hectare site will hold customs, quarantine, immigration and two warehouses, with a possible rail link to India.
The dry port would give a shorter trade route to Indian ports and north-east India, and could draw herbal and food processing industries.
Shuklaphanta National Park and the Mahakali corridor support tourism.
Land services are moving to every local government within a month, which should make registering plots in Bhimdatta simpler.
places.name: Bhimdatta and Dodhara Chandani
risks: Sudurpashchim has among the lowest property deal volumes in the country.
Plans for an industrial zone and the Mahakali corridor have moved slowly, and the Mahakali irrigation project is only about a quarter built.
Factories across Sudurpashchim run at only about half their capacity, and provincial growth was about 3.3% last year.
Plot subdivision has been frozen since mid-July in the 331 of 753 local governments that have not finished land use classification; check whether the municipality you buy in has.
places.signal: The India-funded dry port at Dodhara Chandani (about Rs 2.37 billion in Indian rupees) reached 26% completion by early November 2026, up from about 13% in June, on a 30-month schedule.

Valley plots fell about a third in the 2012 slump.

Steady tourism; the Annapurna region drew nearly 33,000 foreign visitors in Ashoj.

mentor.disclaimer: These are estimates built from published studies of farms that were already running. For each business the main figures were checked against the full paper; where a figure comes from elsewhere, the card says so. A new farm may earn less at first, and prices change. Profit is before income tax and before paying yourself for your own work. Check today's local prices and talk to at least two working farmers before spending money. This is general information, not financial advice.

ideas.name: Banana farm
ideas.where: Terai and inner Terai. The studies are from Chitwan.
ideas.land: {n} kattha of farmland with irrigation. The costs include renting it.
ideas.evidence: A 2025 study of 135 Chitwan banana farms, read in full
ideas.why: A 2025 study of 135 Chitwan banana farms found every size of farm made a profit, about Rs 152 back for every Rs 100 spent, even after paying land rent. There is no shed or pond to build, so your money goes into the crop.
steps: Visit two banana farms nearby and ask what they earned per kattha last year
Find land with irrigation and agree the rent in writing
Line up a buyer or wholesaler before you plant
Buy disease-free plants from a trusted nursery
watch: The first bunches take about a year, so you need money to live on until then.
Costs include about Rs 2,300 per kattha a year for land rent. On land you own, profit is higher by about that much.
Wind, floods and plant disease can wipe out a crop.
ideas.basis: From a 2025 study of 135 Chitwan banana farms: costs of Rs 10,263 per kattha a year (including Rs 2,276 land rent), sales of Rs 15,475, and profit of Rs 5,212. The cautious and good cases are the study's small farms (under 10 kattha, Rs 4,637) and large farms (over 40 kattha, Rs 6,997). No set-up cost is counted beyond the year's costs.

ideas.name: Beekeeping for honey
ideas.where: Terai and mid-hills with flowering crops or forest nearby.
ideas.land: A place to keep {n} hives. Bees feed on other people's crops and forest, so you need little land of your own.
ideas.evidence: A 2026 study of 60 Chitwan beekeepers, read in full, and an earlier Chitwan study
ideas.why: Bees need little land, and a 2026 study of 60 commercial Chitwan beekeepers found Rs 217 back for every Rs 100 spent, with 28 kg of honey per hive a year. An earlier Chitwan study found less, Rs 156, so the cautious case uses that.
steps: Work a honey season with an experienced beekeeper before buying hives
Get a written price for hives with bees from two suppliers
Map where the bees will feed in each season and how you will move them
Agree a buyer for your honey, or plan how to sell it yourself
watch: Bee disease and pests were the worst problem in the 2026 study, followed by pesticide spraying and too little forage.
The Rs 8,000 price for a hive with bees comes from a beekeepers' federation interview, not the study. Check today's price.
The study's beekeepers ran 71 hives on average and most had over 10 years' experience. Start smaller and learn first.
ideas.basis: From a 2026 study of 60 Chitwan beekeepers (data from 2025): running costs of Rs 3,885 per hive a year plus Rs 1,939 of equipment wear, sales of Rs 12,644 (honey at Rs 425 a kg, and beeswax), so profit is Rs 6,821 per hive. The cautious case, Rs 3,300, is from an earlier Chitwan study. Set-up is Rs 8,000 a hive with bees, the price a Federation of Beekeeping Nepal coordinator gave.

sources.name: B360 Nepal: The money in honey

ideas.name: Tomatoes in plastic tunnels
ideas.where: Hills and valleys near a town market. The studies are from the Kathmandu Valley.
ideas.land: About {a} ropani of flat land with water, three tunnels to a ropani. Each tunnel is 28 by 5 metres. The costs include renting the land.
ideas.evidence: A 2024 study of 150 Kathmandu tunnel farms, read in full
ideas.why: A 28 by 5 metre bamboo and plastic tunnel costs about Rs 23,600 to build. A 2024 study of 150 Kathmandu farms found Rs 177 back for every Rs 100 spent, after land rent and tunnel wear.
steps: Visit tunnel farmers nearby and ask what price they got each month last year
Get a quote for one 28 by 5 metre bamboo tunnel with plastic sheet
Check you have water through the dry months
Start with one or two tunnels and add more after the first season
watch: Prices swing a lot. An earlier thesis in Chandragiri recorded Rs 5 to Rs 130 a kilo, and its farmers kept far less than this study's.
These farms sell into the Kathmandu market. Prices and costs elsewhere will differ, so ask local tunnel farmers.
Wind storms can destroy tunnels. Selling when everyone else sells gets the lowest price.
ideas.basis: From a 2024 study of 150 farms in Chandragiri, Tarakeshwar and Kirtipur: a 28 by 5 metre tunnel costs Rs 23,648 to build, and three fit on a ropani. Per hectare a year, costs were Rs 19.8 lakh (including land rent, tunnel wear and loan interest) and profit was Rs 15.5 lakh. We converted these to one tunnel (about 59 to a hectare): costs of about Rs 33,600 and profit of about Rs 26,400 a year. The cautious and good cases are Kirtipur and Tarakeshwar.

sources.name: Journal of Agriculture and Environment 2026, Kathmandu (full paper)

ideas.name: Broiler chicken farm
ideas.where: Near a town with a chick and feed supplier.
ideas.land: A shed of about {n} square feet, away from houses.
ideas.evidence: A study of 120 Rupandehi broiler farms, read in full. Shed cost from Indian project models.
ideas.why: Chickens sell in about six weeks, so money comes back faster than in any other option here. A study of 120 Rupandehi farms found about Rs 100 profit per bird per batch, or Rs 127 back for every Rs 100 spent. That is a thin margin, so one bad batch hurts.
steps: Work a full batch on someone else's farm first
Get written prices for day-old chicks and feed from two suppliers
Get a local quote for the shed, because our figure comes from Indian models
Agree a buyer before the chicks arrive
watch: A drop in the chicken price or a disease outbreak can turn a batch into a loss.
The shed cost is converted from Indian project models at Rs 1.6 per Indian rupee. Get a local quote.
The study's survey is from 2020. Feed and chick prices have changed since.
ideas.basis: From a study of 120 Rupandehi farms (2020 survey): costs of Rs 373 a bird per batch on small farms (under 1,000 birds), sales of Rs 474 (birds, manure and feed bags), so profit is Rs 100 a bird. Medium and large farms made Rs 97 and Rs 117. We assume five batches a year. Shed and equipment are Rs 320 a bird, converted from Indian model projects.

sources.name: Journal of Agriculture and Natural Resources 2023, Rupandehi (full paper)

ideas.name: Carp fish pond
ideas.where: Terai. The studies are from Bara, Kanchanpur, Siraha and Chitwan.
ideas.land: {n} kattha for the pond, plus room for its banks. The costs include renting the land.
ideas.evidence: A study of 90 Bara fish farms, read in full, and a 2025 Kanchanpur study
ideas.why: A study of 90 Bara fish farms found ponds clearly profitable after paying land rent: Rs 167 back for every Rs 100 for table-size carp, and Rs 197 for small "chhari" fish. If you can lease a pond that is already dug, you skip the biggest cost.
steps: Look for an existing pond to lease before paying to dig one
Visit the nearest hatchery and ask about fingerling prices and supply
Get a digging quote for your soil and check the pond will hold water all year
Ask working farmers what feed costs them, since feed is the largest running cost
watch: Digging a new pond is the biggest cost. Lease an existing pond if you can.
In Bara, middlemen set the price, so farmers kept less of the profit.
The cautious case is from a 2025 Kanchanpur study, which found lower returns than Bara.
ideas.basis: From a study of 90 Bara farms (2019 survey): costs of Rs 9.72 lakh per hectare a year, including land rent (21%), feed and labour. Profit per hectare was Rs 6.66 lakh for table-size carp and Rs 9.21 lakh for chhari. We converted these to one kattha (about 29.5 to a hectare): costs of about Rs 32,900 and profit of Rs 22,500 (carp) or Rs 31,200 (chhari). The cautious case applies a 2025 Kanchanpur study's return of Rs 140 per Rs 100 to the same cost. Digging uses a government rate of Rs 93 per cubic metre and a 1.5 metre deep pond.

sources.name: Journal of Agriculture and Natural Resources 2019, Bara (full paper)

ideas.name: Ginger
ideas.where: Mid-hills with upland (bari) fields. The study is from Surkhet.
ideas.land: {n} ropani of upland (bari). Land rent is not counted.
ideas.evidence: A 2026 study of 100 Surkhet ginger growers, read in full
ideas.why: Ginger grows on ordinary upland with no shed or tunnel to build. A 2026 study of 100 growers in Surkhet found Rs 164 back for every Rs 100 spent: about 520 kg a ropani, sold at Rs 35 a kilo.
steps: Talk to two ginger growers and a local trader about this year's price
Buy healthy seed rhizome from a trusted source, since seed is the biggest cost
Plan to store or slice some ginger so you don't have to sell in the harvest rush
Agree a buyer before harvest
watch: Prices swing a lot, and everyone harvests in Asoj and Kartik, when prices are lowest.
Land rent is not counted. If you rent land, profit is lower.
Rhizome rot and other diseases can cut yields sharply.
ideas.basis: From a 2026 study of 100 ginger growers in Bheriganga, Surkhet: costs of Rs 11,061 per ropani a year (seed rhizome 32%, manure 22%), and 520 kg sold at a farm-gate price of Rs 35 a kg for Rs 18,185, so profit is Rs 7,124 per ropani. Only one study gives a profit figure here, so there is no range.

sources.name: Journal of Agriculture and Resource Management 2026, Surkhet (full paper)

ideas.name: Goat farm
ideas.where: Terai and hills, with grazing or fodder land. The study is from Banke.
ideas.land: A dry, raised shed and grazing or fodder land for {n}0 goats. Family labour and home-grown fodder are not counted.
ideas.evidence: A 2025 survey of 95 goat-keeping households in Banke, read in full
ideas.why: Goats sell well at Dashain and Tihar and need little cash to run. A 2025 survey of 95 households in Banke found a 10-goat farm makes about Rs 28,000 a year, Rs 122 back for every Rs 100 spent, when the family does the daily care and grows its own green fodder.
steps: Visit two goat farms and ask what their goats sold for at Dashain
Plan your fodder, since growing your own keeps costs down
Buy healthy does from a known breeder and have a vet check them
Build a dry, raised shed before the animals arrive
watch: The profit counts no pay for the family's daily work. Hiring that work out would wipe out most of it.
Disease and feed costs were farmers' biggest worries in the survey.
Set-up takes about 5 years to earn back at this profit.
ideas.basis: From a 2025 survey of 95 goat-keeping households in Khajura, Banke, worked by the study into a standard 10-goat farm. Setting up costs Rs 60,000 for a shed, Rs 15,000 for equipment and Rs 72,000 for 9 breeding goats. Running costs are Rs 1,02,286 a year (bought feed, vet care, casual labour, water and electricity) plus Rs 2,300 insurance. Selling 8 goats a year at Rs 19,500 brings Rs 1,56,000, so profit after equipment and stock wear is Rs 28,014. Only one study gives a profit figure here, so there is no range.

sources.name: Journal of Agriculture and Forestry University 2026, Banke (full paper)

watch.name: Dairy cows and buffalo
watch.finding: A Chitwan study found cow farms got Rs 144 back for every Rs 100 spent, but buffalo-only farms made a small loss. A Kaski study found the opposite: Rs 181 for buffalo and Rs 118 for cattle. We found no reliable current price for an improved cow, so there is no start-up figure.

watch.name: Large cardamom
watch.finding: A 2018 study of 90 growers in Ilam, Panchthar and Taplejung found it profitable, earning back its set-up in about 4 years. But the first harvest only comes in year 3 or 4, and the price, set largely by Indian buyers, swings widely. Its sums rest on 2017 prices, so we have left the numbers out.

sources.name: Journal of Agriculture and Natural Resources 2018

watch.name: Oyster mushrooms
watch.finding: A Kathmandu Valley study found that returns from mushroom tunnels are falling, and that a tunnel must sell 692 kg just to cover its costs. Recent cost figures come mostly from blogs, so we have left the numbers out.

watch.name: Homestay
watch.finding: In a survey of 22 homestay households in Bardia, the average household earned about Rs 9,000 a month, and those who invested least earned the most back per rupee. The survey is from 2015, so today's costs will be higher.

sectors.note: Sector guides show what it takes to start and the key public numbers. They give no profit estimate, because profit depends on the exact product, place and owner. Registration steps are summarised from official offices and advisers' guides; check the current rules and fees with the office before you apply.

items.name: Farming and agribusiness
items.summary: About a quarter of Nepal's economy. Seven farm businesses in the Mentor above come with costs, profit and first steps sized to your budget.
start: Pick a business above and read its first steps
Talk to two farmers already doing it
Register with your ward or municipality if you will sell regularly
Ask the local agriculture office about subsidies and training
risks: Weather, floods and disease
Prices fall when everyone sells at once
Middlemen take a big share of the price

items.name: Import and export trading
items.summary: Nepal imports far more than it exports, so there is room both for importers and for anyone who can grow exports or make at home what is now imported.

numbers.label: Imports, FY 2082/83
numbers.note: Exports were Rs 315 arba, a gap of Rs 1,781 arba

numbers.label: Biggest import
numbers.note: Rs 297 arba in the first 11 months; exports of soybean oil, cardamom and noodles were growing

start: Register the business: a sole firm or partnership with the Department of Commerce or your municipality, or a company online with the Office of the Company Registrar
Get a PAN from the Inland Revenue Department, and register for VAT if your turnover passes the limit or your trade requires it. Importers are reported to need VAT from the first sale
Get an EXIM code from the Department of Customs through the Nepal National Single Window, and renew it every year
Open a bank account for letters of credit and foreign payments, and find a customs agent
Start with one product and one supplier you can visit
risks: Customs duties and rules change with each budget
Competition from goods brought in informally across the open border
Forex and payment rules: payments must go through banks

items.name: Retail shop and wholesale
items.summary: Spending drives Nepal's economy, so shops, distributors and wholesalers are everywhere. Margins are thin, and location and stock control decide who survives.
start: Register the business: a sole firm or partnership with the Department of Commerce or your municipality, or a company online with the Office of the Company Registrar

Get a PAN from the Inland Revenue Department, and register for VAT if your turnover passes the limit or your trade requires it. Advisers report the VAT limit at Rs 30 lakh turnover for services and mixed businesses; check with the tax office
Register with your ward or municipality and renew each year
Agree credit terms with two suppliers before you stock up
Keep daily sales and stock records from day one
risks: Selling on credit (udharo) ties up your cash
Rent and slow-moving stock eat thin margins
Competition from online sellers and bigger stores

items.name: IT and online services
items.summary: Software, design, data and online work sold abroad bring dollars into Nepal with little start-up money. Skill and reliable delivery are the main capital.
start: Build a portfolio of three real projects
Register as a firm or company and get a PAN once clients pay regularly
Receive payments through a bank so the income counts as an export and stays legal
Start with one client market and one service you do well
risks: Global competition on price
Receiving foreign payments can be slow; informal channels such as hundi are illegal
Client concentration: losing one big client hurts

items.name: Tourism and hospitality
items.summary: Homestays, guiding, trekking agencies, hotels and restaurants. Arrivals are back above one million a year, but the season and a few big markets decide the year.

numbers.label: Foreign tourists, 2025
numbers.note: Up about 1% on 2024; India the largest market (Nepal Tourism Board)

start: Homestay: register with your municipality or province under local homestay rules
Trekking or travel agency: register a company, get PAN and VAT, then a licence from the Department of Tourism. It needs an office and licensed guides
Advisers report a deposit and capital requirement for agencies; confirm the current amounts with the Department of Tourism
List on booking sites and ask every guest for a review
risks: Seasons: spring and autumn carry the year
Disasters, strikes or a bad news story can empty bookings
Dependence on a few source countries

items.name: Small manufacturing and food processing
items.summary: Making at home what Nepal now imports: food, packaging, furniture, construction materials. Industry is a small slice of the economy, which leaves room to grow.
start: Register the industry with the Department of Cottage and Small Industries (cottage and small) or the Department of Industry (larger)
Get a PAN from the Inland Revenue Department, and register for VAT if your turnover passes the limit or your trade requires it
For food products, get a licence from the Department of Food Technology and Quality Control
Test-sell a small batch to shops before buying machines
risks: Cheaper imports from India and China
Power cuts in the dry season
Working capital tied up in raw materials and unpaid invoices

sources.name: Department of Cottage and Small Industries

items.name: Construction and real estate
items.summary: Building, contracting, materials and land. Big projects and towns keep demand going, but payments are often late and land prices move slowly.

numbers.label: Economic growth, FY 2082/83
numbers.note: Expected; construction and manufacturing were under pressure

start: Contractors need a construction business licence in the class that matches the size of work
Register the business: a sole firm or partnership with the Department of Commerce or your municipality, or a company online with the Office of the Company Registrar
For land, read the Places section in the Invest tab first
Never pay for land before checking the ownership papers at the land revenue office
risks: Late payment on government work
Cement and steel price swings
Monsoon stops sites for months

items.name: Transport and logistics
items.summary: Moving goods and people: trucks, buses, delivery, warehousing and customs clearing. Every imported item has to be moved, so steady demand follows trade.
start: Register the business: a sole firm or partnership with the Department of Commerce or your municipality, or a company online with the Office of the Company Registrar
Get vehicle registration and route permits from the transport management office
Get a PAN from the Inland Revenue Department, and register for VAT if your turnover passes the limit or your trade requires it
Insure every vehicle and load
Start with one route or one regular customer
risks: Fuel prices
Road closures in the monsoon
Route syndicates and permit delays

items.name: Education and training
items.summary: Schools, coaching, language classes and skills training. Private schools keep growing, but a new law brings fee rules and scholarship quotas.
start: A school needs approval from the local government under education law, and registers as a company or a trust
Coaching or training: register a firm, get a PAN, and check local permission rules
Vocational courses can seek CTEVT affiliation
Start with one subject or skill where results are easy to show
risks: Fee rules and scholarship quotas under the new school law
Staff turnover
Reputation spreads by word of mouth, both ways

items.name: Health and pharmacy
items.summary: Pharmacies, clinics, labs and care services. Demand is steady everywhere, but this sector is the most tightly licensed.
start: A pharmacy needs a licence from the Department of Drug Administration under the Drug Act, and a registered pharmacist or assistant pharmacist
Clinics and labs need approval from the health authorities; confirm the current rules with the Ministry of Health and Population or your province
Register the business: a sole firm or partnership with the Department of Commerce or your municipality, or a company online with the Office of the Company Registrar
Plan premises to meet the standards that are inspected
risks: Licences can be suspended for breaking rules
Medicine price controls
Qualified staff are hard to keep in rural areas

items.name: Energy and hydropower
items.summary: Nepal's biggest long-term bet. Small businesses can install solar and electrical systems; savers mostly take part by buying hydropower shares.

numbers.label: Electricity exports, FY 2025/26
numbers.note: 3.88 billion units sold to India and Bangladesh; a net electricity trade surplus of Rs 18.76 arba

start: Solar or electrical contracting: register a firm, get a PAN, and hire licensed electricians
To invest instead, see the hydropower sector in the NEPSE tab
Apply for hydropower IPOs through MeroShare once you have a demat account
risks: Floods: 13 projects in the Trishuli valley were damaged in 2026
Dry-season shortages and imports
Hydropower shares swing widely

items.name: Finance, savings and cooperatives
items.summary: Banks, insurers and cooperatives. Starting one needs a licence and large capital, so most people take part as savers, agents or investors.

numbers.label: Savings stuck in troubled cooperatives
numbers.note: Owed to about 76,000 depositors in 2026; refunds are slow

start: To save, compare fixed deposits and bonds in the Invest tab
Before putting money in a cooperative, check it is registered and ask for its latest audited accounts
Agent work (insurance, remittance) needs a licence from the regulator for that service
risks: Cooperative failures: savings above Rs 5 lakh were not covered by the 2026 refund order
Promises of unusually high interest are a warning sign
Only Nepal Rastra Bank licensed banks and finance companies take public deposits

items.name: Investing in shares by sector
items.summary: Owning part of Nepali companies through NEPSE: banks, hydropower, insurance, microfinance, manufacturing and more. Returns swing from year to year.

numbers.label: NEPSE, FY 2082/83
numbers.note: Closed at 2,597.80, after rising 24.74% the year before

start: Open a demat account and MeroShare login with a depository participant (most banks offer this)
Open a trading account with a licensed broker
Start with IPOs and a few sectors you understand; see today's sector moves in the NEPSE tab
risks: Share prices can fall a long way
Hype and tips on social media
Money you need within a few years is safer in a fixed deposit
